Subject: Elevated 5xx / timeouts from redwood-base-v2 in production

Hi Jonas —

We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and request timeouts hitting our production routes that use model 'redwood-base-v2' (api model id: redwood-base-v2). Error rates climbed sharply around 08:45 PST and have stayed elevated (~6–9% 5xx across endpoints). Latency for success responses has also increased. We implemented client-side retries but it isn't enough for user-facing flows.

Attached: small sample of request IDs and timestamps (request_sample_logs.txt).

Can you confirm whether there is an ongoing issue on your side and if there is a recommended temporary mitigation (fallback model, rate limit change, etc.)? This is impacting a subset of our customers.

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:40:22 -08:00
Subject: Internal: redwood-base-v2 elevated 5xx — preliminary findings

Internal summary (not for customer):
- Timeline: error spike correlated with a rolling kernel-level deployment to the inference runtime fleet between 08:30–08:38 PST.
- Symptom: increased 5xx (HTTP 503 / inference timeouts) driven by excessive memory fragmentation under specific request size patterns; certain long-context requests triggered fallback paths that timed out under kernel memory contention.
- Impact surface: ~3% of total requests globally for redwood-base-v2; higher for the tenant in this thread (~7%).
- Immediate mitigation applied: rolled back the kernel patch on the affected ASG and forced a graceful restart of the GPUs in that pool. Also routed traffic for ACME to redwood-base-v2-compat while we confirm stability.

Attachments: request_sample_logs.txt (original from ACME), incident_graphs_20260215.png (error rate graphs), kernel-deploy-diff.txt (internal).

Next steps:
1) Continue monitoring error rates for 60–90 minutes post-rollback.
2) Run a synthetic job matching ACME's request profile to validate KV cache behavior.
3) Prepare a patch to ensure the runtime uses a conservative memory allocator for long-context workloads (target: hotfix by EOD).

— Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: redwood-base-v2 — error rates trending down (rollback applied)

Hi Samantha — quick update on the incident.

What we did:
- Identified a recent runtime kernel change that increased memory fragmentation for long-context requests.
- Rolled back the kernel patch on the affected serving pool and performed a graceful restart of the GPUs.
- Kept your traffic on redwood-base-v2-compat for safe fallback during validation.

Current status (13:00 PST):
- Error rates for your account are down to ~0.4% (from ~7% at peak).
- Overall error spike for redwood-base-v2 has subsided and rolling averages are within normal bounds.

Attachments: incident_graphs_20260215.png (error timeline), request_sample_logs.txt (annotated).

Next steps and timeline:
- We will run targeted synthetic tests matching your request mix for the next 2 hours and monitor.
- Dev's team will deploy a conservative allocator patch to the runtime (hotfix planned for EOD) and we'll test in canary before re-enabling the original model route.
- I will share a formal postmortem within 48 hours that includes root cause analysis, a timeline, and compensatory actions.

Apologies again for the disruption. Laura from our CS team will follow up on any product/credit requests to make this right.

Best,
Jonas Weber
